clue.text: Ancient old boy rebuffed in the wine shop

indicators.note: rebuffed means pushed back, so the whole run of letters from ancient old boy is read backwards

parts.note: ancient means aged, very old
OB is the standard abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A former pupil, now elderly, is turned away at the door of a wine shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuffed' turns the whole of AGED + OB backwards, giving BO + DEGA.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodega is a Spanish-style cellar or shop selling wine.

clue.text: Dialect players in The Archers, perhaps?

parts.note: broad speech is strong regional dialect
the cast are the actors in a production

explanation.surface: Actors in the radio soap speak in rural dialect.
explanation.walkthrough: The Archers is a long-running BBC radio soap set in a farming village.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio serial is an example of a programme transmitted over the air.

clue.text: Digger clearing the bed

parts.note: the bed suggests sheets and pillows, but it is the bottom of a river or harbour being scooped out

explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' tempts as somewhere to sleep; it is a riverbed.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel or machine that scoops silt from waterways is named for that dredging work.

clue.text: The toiler has to hold his nose here

definitions.text: The toiler has to hold his nose here

parts.words: The toiler has to hold his nose here
parts.note: the idiom of keeping your nose pressed to a sharpening wheel means working hard without a break

explanation.walkthrough: 'hold his nose' suggests a bad smell; it is the idiom 'keep your nose to the ...'.
explanation.definitionFit: A revolving stone for sharpening tools gives the idiom for relentless hard work.

clue.text: One who heard from Paul — for the record, he's a Scots boy

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
taken as written, without the apostrophe
Ian is a typical Scottish boy's name

explanation.surface: A biblical aside: a man who received a letter from St Paul is, for the record, a Scottish lad.
explanation.walkthrough: St Paul wrote the Epistle to the Ephesians, so a member of that church at Ephesus heard from Paul.
explanation.definitionFit: The people of Ephesus received one of Paul's New Testament letters, so each was a recipient of his epistle.

clue.text: This shark is nothing less than a rotten spy

indicators.note: less than signals that what comes before is subtracted from the word after

parts.note: rotten means poor, of bad quality
O looks like zero, nothing
a beagle is slang for a spy or detective, after the hunting dog

explanation.surface: A shark is dismissed as nothing more than a lousy secret agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less than' takes O (nothing) out of POOR, leaving POR.
explanation.definitionFit: A porbeagle is a mackerel shark of the North Atlantic.

clue.text: Where else could you find such slippery people?

indicators.note: asking where you could find them points to letters sitting inside the words where else

explanation.surface: Someone asks where else such shifty characters might turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the join of 'wherE ELSe'.
explanation.definitionFit: Slippery, evasive people are called eels, after the hard-to-hold fish.

clue.text: One member learning to conjure

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
MP is a Member of Parliament
lore is traditional knowledge or learning

explanation.surface: A single club member is studying the art of magic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conjure' suggests magic tricks, but its older sense is to beg solemnly.
explanation.definitionFit: To conjure someone, in the old sense, is to beseech or entreat them earnestly.

clue.text: That's cold in Durham for a girl!

indicators.note: in places i.e. and the letter for cold inside the abbreviation for the north-east

parts.note: Durham is in north-east England, NE
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A remark about the chilly weather in the north-east of England, said of a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Durham is a county and city in north-east England; 'That's' gives IE (that is).
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a female relative, so a girl in family terms.

clue.text: Arms king in France

definitions.meaning: the Lord ... King of Arms is Scotland's chief heraldic officer
a city in France, on the Rhône

explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish herald's title includes the name, and the same word is the French city on the Rhône and Saône.

clue.text: The result of attaching too much weight to the so-called place of honour

definitions.text: The result of attaching too much weight

parts.note: OBE (Order of the British Empire) is a British honour

indicators.note: so-called here means the word for place is only as it is called aloud, giving its sound not its spelling

parts.note: a city is a place, a town

explanation.surface: A grand dignitary piles on too much weight in the seat of honour.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is a British honour awarded by the monarch; CITY is said aloud and written SITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Excess body fat is what comes of putting on too many pounds: a medical condition of overweight.

clue.text: To fall back is a mistake by soldiers

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a common crossword name for soldiers
a lapse is a slip or minor error

explanation.surface: Retreating is a blunder made by the troops.
explanation.definitionFit: To relapse is to slide back into a former state, especially illness.

clue.text: Chow-chow? What a mess!

definitions.meaning: chow is a dog breed and chow is slang for food, so a chow's chow is a hound's meal
a ... is British slang for a muddle or shambles

explanation.surface: Someone sees a plate of dog food and exclaims at the state of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet's meal is the literal sense; the idiom means a botched, untidy job.

clue.text: Arch fellow

definitions.meaning: a concave arch or arched moulding in building
old British slang for a man, a chap

explanation.definitionFit: In architecture the word names a curved vault; in slang it names a chap or bloke.

clue.text: No treaty is amended in pen and ink, for example

indicators.note: amended means altered, so the letters of no treaty is are rewritten in a new order

explanation.surface: A treaty is not amended in its written text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amended' rearranges NOTREATYIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing materials such as pens and ink are examples of office supplies of this kind.

clue.text: It makes bubbles to amuse, say, the king

parts.note: read amuse as 'a muse', and Erato, Muse of lyric poetry, is an example, giving A + ERATO
R stands for rex, king

explanation.surface: Something fizzy is laid on to entertain a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amuse' splits into 'a muse'; 'say' marks Erato as one example of the nine Muses.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that pumps air into liquid, as in a fish tank, produces a stream of bubbles.

clue.text: Go to the country — a trick to contain silent uprising

indicators.note: to contain means the trick holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a ruse is a trick

indicators.note: uprising in a down clue means the word for silent is read from bottom to top

parts.note: tacit means unspoken, silent

explanation.surface: A political plea to head for the countryside before a quiet rebellion breaks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' turns TACIT into TICAT, and 'to contain' puts it inside RUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rusticate is to retire to or live in rural parts.

clue.text: Concludes contracts

definitions.meaning: to gather is to infer, as in 'I gather you're leaving'
to gather fabric is to draw it together into folds

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is deducing from evidence; the other is drawing cloth or a brow tightly together.

clue.text: Guardsman's home makes second appearance on the telly

parts.note: an entry is an appearance, a coming on
the box is British slang for television

explanation.surface: A soldier's shelter turns up for a second time on TV.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second appearance' looks like a repeat showing; it splits into S and ENTRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry box is a small hut sheltering a soldier on guard duty.

clue.text: Volunteers sovereigns from the receipts

parts.note: TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force
sovereigns are monarchs, kings

explanation.surface: Volunteer soldiers take gold coins out of the day's earnings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sovereigns' tempts as old gold coins, which would suit receipts; it means monarchs.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop's takings are the money it has received over a period.

clue.text: Criticised hit

definitions.meaning: to knock something is to run it down, disparage it

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is finding fault verbally; the other is striking with a blow.

clue.text: Begin to deal with the alimentary canal

definitions.meaning: to ... a task is to start tackling it
the gut running from mouth to anus; the anatomists' term

explanation.surface: Someone starts tackling a medical subject: the digestive tract.
explanation.definitionFit: As a phrasal verb it means embark upon; as one zoological word it means the gut.

clue.text: Ruling needed for admission of girl to the regiment

indicators.note: admission of means the girl is let inside the regiment

parts.note: REGT is the abbreviation for regiment
Nan is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Admitting a woman to the regiment requires an official ruling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruling' looks like a noun, a decision, but is the adjective meaning reigning.
explanation.definitionFit: Regnant describes a monarch reigning in their own right, as in queen regnant.

clue.text: It sounds like a clique in this club

definitions.text: It sounds like a clique in this club

parts.words: It sounds like a clique in this club
parts.note: the old Scottish golf club called a cleek, pronounced like clique, belongs to the family of metal-headed clubs

explanation.walkthrough: A cleek is an old name for a golf club with a metal head; it rhymes with the French-style 'clique' pronunciation.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf club with a metal head is named for the metal it was once forged from.

clue.text: Male in Shakespearian role makes ideal picture

indicators.note: in puts the letter for male inside the name of the villain

parts.note: Iago is the villain of Othello

explanation.surface: A man playing a Shakespeare part looks the perfect picture.
explanation.walkthrough: IAGO is the schemer in Shakespeare's Othello.
explanation.definitionFit: In psychoanalysis an imago is an idealised mental image of a person, often a parent.

clue.text: Sole dealer, as Hamlet knew Polonius to be

definitions.meaning: a seller of sole and other fish, sole being a flatfish

definitions.text: as Hamlet knew Polonius to be
definitions.meaning: in Act 2 of Hamlet the prince, feigning madness

explanation.surface: A trader in one item is compared with Polonius as Hamlet saw him.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman selling fish deals in sole; Hamlet mockingly gives Polonius that trade.

clue.text: Tilt horse, one of 6

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H
6 down is the slippery fish, so one of them is a single eel

explanation.surface: A jousting horse is one of six in the lists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' gives H via heroin slang; '6' points to 6-down.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship heels when it leans over to one side.

clue.text: Island Premier overturned by single band of warriors

indicators.note: overturned in a down clue means the letters for premier are flipped upside down

parts.note: PM is Prime Minister, the premier
I is the Roman numeral one, single

explanation.surface: An island's prime minister is ousted by a lone band of fighters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' turns PM into MP.
explanation.definitionFit: An impi was a Zulu regiment or armed force.

clue.text: It signals the morning

parts.note: old British military signallers spelt out the letters A and M with code words, so the forenoon had a signalese name

explanation.walkthrough: Before the modern phonetic alphabet, British signallers said Ack for A and Emma for M.
explanation.definitionFit: In the old signalling alphabet the two letters standing for ante meridiem denote the forenoon.

clue.text: We are not without blame for smashing cherished possession

indicators.note: smashing breaks the words we and blame apart so their letters can be rebuilt

explanation.surface: We admit some guilt for breaking something treasured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are not without' just means 'with', joining the two fodder words; 'smashing' rearranges WE and BLAME.
explanation.definitionFit: In Nathan's parable in Samuel, a poor man's one little lamb is his treasured property, hence the phrase for a dearest possession.

clue.text: Bishop and legislator

definitions.meaning: a bishop is one who ordains priests
to ordain is also to decree or enact a law

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a cleric conferring holy orders; the other is someone who decrees laws.

clue.text: The rules governing sentences for an offence reported by Customs

indicators.note: reported means the word for an offence is passed on by voice, so only its sound counts

parts.note: a sin is a moral offence
customs are duties, a tax on goods

explanation.surface: A rulebook for prison terms, handed down for a crime the customs officers have reported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sentences' looks like jail terms but means grammatical sentences; SIN said aloud is written SYN.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar's arrangement of words into clauses is governed by syntax.
